description.narrative: Reporting is an important management tool which is used to inform relevant government officials and other stakeholders about the results being achieved by individual projects and the programme as a whole. For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities . Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the grant award letter, the dates for submission of the annual reports are mentioned. In case of a three-year project, between 5-7 reports are obligatory. The first report (0) is a very short report which focuses on specific conditions and/or recommendations in the grant. There is no need to report on progress in achieving outputs and outcomes, which is done in the first annual report. As annex to the report 0, the consortium agreements between the partners should be submitted. The final report must reflect on the entire project period.

In this section (maximum 1000 words), please provide a global overview of the project progress **per output**. To what extent have they been achieved? Comment on the activities that have taken place and the most important milestones.

actual.value:
The implementation of the TMT Mantis and all the modules was achieved completely. The objectives were fully met and based on the feedback provided by the participants 86% considered that the course was between very good and good. The TMT was delivered by implementing 3 modules. The first two modules were implemented remotely online using the virtual campus and learning environment facilitated by IHE. These two modules were implemented during 2-3 weeks’ time as agreed between the requesting and implementing organizations. This was done considering the time zone difference between Colombia and the Netherlands and also the modality of the teaching and training activities. The methodology used in the training consisted of a mix of lectures, teaching material, readings, slides, software manuals and guidelines, software tools (for example each participant were given a license of ArcGIS valid for one year), case studies (a mix of cases were used including case studies facilitated by the requesting organization in Medellin), individual project and presentation as well as group discussion and feedback. The third and last module was implemented in a hybrid modality some days were done remotely online and other days were done face to face at the premises of EPM in Medellin. The three modules can be summarized as follows: Module I - Data Collection and Processing for Modelling purposes Modality remotely online Implemented time: 18- 29 January 2021.
This module provided an overview of data needs, data collection, sources and processing with GIS for modelling purposes. In particular, integration of spatial data for flood assessment and analysis. The module focused on processing spatial data with the use of ArcGIS tool. Experiences and case studies from the Netherlands and Europe were also presented by the Dutch SME Interact. In particular the integration of data for monitoring and real time decision making for operation and management of flood gates, weirs and pumps with the purpose of flood mitigation.
Module II Methods and tools for the analysis of Urban floods Modality remotely online Implemented time: 12 – 26 April 20. This module presented the integration of the topics presented in module and their use for modelling purposes. The module included lectures with theoretical explanation and concepts as a foundational knowledge for modelling of urban floods. For the understanding of hydrological process a local case study was used from La Heliodora basin in Envigado (Aburrra Valley area). The data was collected by sensors from SIATA and with other information from EPM a hydrological model was developed and used to practice the acquired knowledge. Several practical exercises of different options for modeling (1d, 2d) were carried out. With the use of the computational software Mike Urban a 1d-2d modeling was performed from an international case study. The outputs of the model where then processed in ArcGIS using the acquired knowledge of module 1 to obtain maps of flood hazard, vulnerability and flood risks. The analysis allowed the participants not only to exercise and practice what was discussed in class but also to understand the problem and the multiple consequences around urban floods.
- Module III - Decision making - searching for multi-functional solutions - Modality Hybrid – online and face to face - Implemented time: 15-26 November 2021 During this module various methodologies of teaching were used, lectures, group work and group discussion as well as individual projects and presentation with plenary discussion and feedback. The individual work consisted in the documentation of a nature based solution in the format of a fact sheet, for which several reading materials and resources from internet were used. Each student needed to prepare a poster, the posters were printed and presented and discussed in plenary. For the group work two case studies were used. The case studies were located in the Aburra Valley, one was the Heliodora basin and consisted of a river model developed by EPM in Hec Ras and it was used to analyze the effect of implementing NBS measures to protect the main sewer collectors from floods, scouring and landslides as a way to protect the environment from raw wastewater leakages; the second case study was the expansion of an urban area in La Estrella and its impact in the existing combined urban drainage and sewerage system. The case study allowed the assessment of flooding and its mitigation by the use of several NBS measures at urban scale. Each group needed to present their findings and discussion in plenary. During Module 3 the municipality of Medellin presented the formulation of the re-naturalization of the Aburra Valley plan (Greening the city) and it was also identified and agreed to have a field visit to see the implementation of some NBS measures in marginalized and vulnerable neighborhoods in Medellin and to evidence the multiple benefits that has been achieved by the Municipal authorities. The field visit was facilitated by EPM and the Medellin municipality jointly. It was an important moment in the TMT as it serves to facilitate multiple discussions and to identify the need for mutual collaboration, enhance communication and sharing of data and information among the institutions involved in the TMT Mantis.
